units.text: Leaflet fracture and escape from an On-X mechanical mitral valve in a child: A case report
October 2021
Introduction
Leaflet escape is a rare but known complication of mechanical valve prostheses
Most commonly reported with the Bjork-Shiley convexo-concave tilting disc prosthesis – 3.9% cumulative incidence1
Four previous reports of leaflet escape from an On-X mechanical valve – two deaths2-5
Timely diagnosis facilitates early referral for valve replacement and increases the chance of survival
Case Presentation
History and Examination Findings
12-year-old boy presents to regional emergency department with acute-onset dyspnoea whilst diving into shallow water
Background of rheumatic heart disease
Status post mitral valve replacement with 25mm On-X valve 1 year prior to presentation
Warfarin to maintain international normalised ratio (INR) 2-3
On examination – RR 60, HR 140, SpO2 70% in air  93% in 15L oxygen
Coughing up pink frothy sputum
Bilateral crepitations to mid-zones
Case Presentation
Investigations
ECG – sinus tachycardia, left ventricular strain
Blood gas - pH 7.37, CO2 5, base excess -3, lactate 2.6
Haemoglobin 159, white cell count 29, platelets 567
Na+ 139, Urea 5.4, Creatinine 89
INR – 2.7
Troponin T – 85ng/L (N <15)
Figure 1. Erect anteroposterior chest radiograph demonstrating bilateral alveolar opacities consistent with pulmonary oedema
Case Presentation
Investigations
Transthoracic echocardiogram
Limited by poor acoustic windows
Mitral valve in-flow gradient 20mmHg
Hyperdynamic left ventricular systolic function
Insufficient tricuspid regurgitation to estimate right ventricular pressure, no obvious pulmonary hypertension
Transoesophageal echocardiogram

Figure 2. Three dimensional transoesophageal echocardiogram of the mitral valve viewed from the left atrium in ventricular diastole (A) and systole (B) demonstrating a single mechanical valve leaflet.

Figure 3. Mid-oesophageal four chamber view from transoesophageal echocardiogram with colour compare in ventricular diastole (A) and systole (B) demonstrating single moving leaflet with resultant severe mitral regurgitation.
Case Presentation
Management
Urgent surgery for mitral valve replacement
On-X valve explanted – single leaflet present, other leaflet not seen in left atrium or left ventricle
Computed tomography scan of chest/abdomen/pelvis 3 days post-operatively - fractured leaflet in descending aorta
Discharged home 14 days after presentation, leaflet fragments remain in-situ
Figure 4. Coronal computed tomography scan demonstrating leaflet fragments (arrows) in the descending aorta and right common iliac artery.
Discussion
Diagnosis – leaflet fracture and escape from On-X mechanical mitral valve
Rare but potentially lethal complication
Risk factors for this complication remain largely unknown given small number of reports
The diagnosis was quickly and easily achieved with transoesophageal echocardiography
Alternative diagnostic modalities include fluoroscopy or cardiac CT
Leaflet fragments left in-situ – an area of contention
Learning Points
Leaflet fracture and escape should be considered when a patient with a mechanical valve presents with sudden-onset haemodynamic or respiratory compromise.
When available, transoesophageal echocardiography should be used as the first line modality for diagnosis of leaflet escape from a mechanical valve.
If recognised promptly, urgent valve replacement can be performed resulting in survival
References
Blot WJ, Ibrahim MA, Ivey TD, et al. Twenty-five-year experience with the Björk-Shiley convexoconcave heart valve: a continuing clinical concern. Circulation. 2005;111(21):2850-7.
Kageyama S, Yoshioka D, Kawasumi R, Ohashi T. Sudden haemodynamic collapse caused by leaflet escape of the contemporary On-X mechanical valve. Eur J Cardiothorac Surg. 2018;54(3):608.
Rivera CA, López Rodríguez FJ, García MEA, et al. Survival After Mitral Valve Replacement for Leaflet Escape in a Contemporary On-X Mechanical Valve. Ann Thorac Surg. 2019;108(5):e307-e9.
Göbel N, Tanriverdi S, Nagib R, Franke UFW. Cardiogenic Shock Due to Leaflet Migration of On-X Aortic Mechanical Prosthesis. Ann Thorac Surg. 2020;110(3):e199-e200.
Helgeland E, Andresen K, Dumont KA, Bjørnstad JL. Leaflet fracture and embolization from an On-X mechanical mitral valve. JTCVS Tech. 2020;3:140-3.

limitations: Structured extraction covers vital signs, laboratory values, anticoagulation target, echocardiographic gradient, CT result and printed on-screen heart rates; narrative slides, background and discussion are not extracted.

The slide set holds patient data absent from the article and values conflicting with it (room-air oxygen saturation, INR target, INR on presentation, embolised-fragment location); conflicting items are review_only and unresolved.
Slide-set provenance of the case is taken from the article statement about the slide set, not from any identifier on the slides.
